intro_seen.description: Player has seen the waking-on-the-beach narration.

shingle_met_pell.description: Player has met Pell on Shingle Point.

saltmarrow_met_mara.description: Player has met Mara Tollen, the harbormaster.

saltmarrow_mara_told_of_dunstan.description: Mara told the player her brother Dunstan walked into the fog.

saltmarrow_met_aldous.description: Player has met Brother Aldous Wren.

saltmarrow_pebble_fate.description: What the player did with the humming pebble Remnant: '' (not decided), 'given' (to Pell) or 'kept'. Pays off when the Gull's Beacon needs a memory to burn.

saltmarrow_aldous_approach.description: How the player first handled Aldous's evasions: '' / 'gentle' / 'pressed'. Gentle earns his trust (he confides sooner in Act I); pressed makes him defensive.

saltmarrow_hesk_saw_dunstan.description: Old Hesk, Hushed in the net-lofts, told the player a big man with a lantern and 'Tollen shoulders' went north laughing, saying he'd come back for his name.

saltmarrow_mara_knows_dunstan_chose.description: Player told Mara what Hesk saw: Dunstan went into the fog willingly. Pays off when Dunstan is found among the Unmoored (Act II).

saltmarrow_pell_lent_pebble.description: Pell agreed to hand the humming pebble back so the Gull's Beacon could burn it. Stays true even if the player later returns it.

saltmarrow_mara_offered_gull.description: Mara held Dunstan's whittled gull in the fog until it became a Remnant of her memory of him, and gave it to the player for the beacon.

saltmarrow_beacon_burned.description: Which Remnant fed the Gull's Beacon: '' (unlit), 'pebble' (the lullaby — Mara's song, Pell's comfort), 'knot' (Saltmarrow's founding knot) or 'gull' (Mara's memory of her brother Dunstan). The Act I choice; Saltmarrow forgets it for good.

saltmarrow_mara_saw_beacon_lit.description: Player has spoken with Mara after the Gull's Beacon was relit (one-time aftermath scene).

saltmarrow_aldous_balked.description: After the beacon was lit, a player who had not been gentle with Aldous asked for his story; he refused and sent them away. Unlocks showing him the ember on the next visit.

saltmarrow_aldous_novice.description: Asked Aldous about the novice on the east stair (Day 47, The East Stair; needs thornwold_lamp_name=told): '' (not yet), 'lamp' (asked for Wynn's sake: he sends his sorry) or 'self' (asked 'could it have been me?': he can't find the player's face anywhere, on the stair or off it). Either way he counts six novices and a seventh with no face, tells of the novices' roll in the warden's niche at the foot of the east stair, and lays the Wrens' brazier.

saltmarrow_aldous_confessed.description: Aldous's Act I confession: '' (untold), 'full' (gentle — the High Keeper put the flame out, a light went down the stair past him, gives the Keeper's sleeve-ember) or 'grudging' (pressed — the bare fact only). Keepers in Act II should know which.

saltmarrow_ferry_lantern_hung.description: Mara hung the green signal lantern on the Saltmarrow dock-post so the Tidewright ferry knows passengers are waiting (Act II bridge).

saltmarrow_pell_ferry_ask.description: What the player told Pell about the ferry: '' (not asked), 'promised' (Pell may come), 'refused' (Pell stays; asks for something lost brought back) or 'undecided' (Pell asks again, loudly, when the ferry comes). Asked on seeing the green lantern or on the dock when the ferry is in.

saltmarrow_mara_saw_sleeve_ember.description: Player showed Mara the Keeper's sleeve-ember Aldous cut from his robe; she warned them Tidewrights don't love Keepers.

saltmarrow_ferry_arrived.description: The Tidewright ferry Slow Mercy sounded its horn and put in at the Saltmarrow dock (region arrival event after the green lantern was hung). Pell moves from Shingle Point to the dock.

saltmarrow_ferry_deed.description: How the player told Oda Farrow their deed (the Tidewright fare): '' (not yet), 'claimed' (I relit the Gull), 'shared' (Saltmarrow did; I carried the ember) or 'brusque' (just take me across). Tidewrights in Act II should know how the Wakebearer talks about their deeds.

saltmarrow_oda_knew_dunstan.description: After the gull burn, Oda Farrow (from off-island) spoke of Dunstan Tollen, who crewed for her; the name would not stay with the Wakebearer. Proof that a burned memory survives off the island (Act II payoff).

saltmarrow_oda_saw_sleeve_ember.description: Player showed Oda Farrow the Keeper's sleeve-ember despite Mara's warning; Tidewrights make Keepers pay twice. Act II Tidewrights may be cooler.

saltmarrow_pell_crossing.description: How Pell's wish to cross ended when the ferry came: '' (unresolved), 'aboard' (Mara gave leave; Pell crosses on the Slow Mercy), 'stayed' (Pell stays and gave the player a finding pouch) or 'let_down' (promised, then the player told Mara Pell should stay). Act II must honour it.

saltmarrow_mara_farewell.description: Mara said goodbye to the player after the ferry's horn (one-time scene).

saltmarrow_mara_message_for_dunstan.description: Mara, knowing Dunstan chose the fog, asked the player to tell him the stool is still there, if they see him. Delivered in person at the end of the long walk (Day 37).

saltmarrow_ferry_passage.description: Oda Farrow gave the player a berth on the Slow Mercy for Thornwold, sailing on the evening tide. Ends Act I (the act-end card); Act II starts from it.

lanes_ferry_at.description: Where the Slow Mercy lies after the crossing: '' (not sailed yet: at the Saltmarrow dock once arrived), 'thornwold' (moored at Thornwold landing), 'saltmarrow' (back at the Saltmarrow dock) 'fen' (at Glasswater Fen's staithe, Day 29) or 'wrackholm' (at Wrackholm's jetty, Day 40). Oda and the ferry prop are placed by it; the player travels with her.

thornwold_landed.description: The player has come ashore at Thornwold landing (one-time arrival scene after the crossing).

thornwold_pell_landed.description: Pell crossed on the Slow Mercy (saltmarrow_pell_crossing=aboard) and stays at Thornwold's lumber camp, sorting Bram's nails. Moves Pell off the Saltmarrow dock.

thornwold_met_bram.description: Player has met Bram Kettle, foreman of the Tidewright lumber camp at Thornwold landing.

thornwold_bram_knot_grudge.description: Bram Kettle (Saltmarrow-born mother, Tidewright) holds the burning of the founding knot against the player. Tidewright net-makers' resentment of the knot burn (LORE); later Tidewrights may share it.

thornwold_bramble_parted.description: The Wakebearer held the ember to the bramble wall and the canes drew back from it, opening a gap onto the cart road behind. The way into the woods past the wall (through the bramble wall's dialogue).

thornwold_woods_entered.description: Player has seen the arrival scene in the woods past the bramble wall (one-time).

thornwold_met_hob.description: Player has met Hob Marl, the last collier on the near side of the ridge, in the clearing past the bramble wall. He brings the sacks down by the lanterns.

thornwold_hob_stick.description: Player told Hob Marl that Pell found a tally stick by the sacks; it is his ('the night I forgot what I was counting') and he lets Pell keep it. Pell can be told whose it is.

thornwold_hob_paid.description: Player carried Bram's salt crock to Hob Marl: the colliers' first pay since the third load. Bram's tally board gets its fourth salt notch and Hob remembers Bram.

thornwold_ladder_stood.description: The Wakebearer stood the Keepers' fallen ladder back against the last pitch above the stair's landing in the woods. The way up to the ridge (climbing it travels to thornwold_ridge).

thornwold_ridge_reached.description: Player has seen the arrival scene on Thornwold's ridge (one-time, after first climbing the ladder).

thornwold_met_lamp.description: Player has met the Lamp at the lantern bench by the keeper's lodge on the ridge (advances A Light for Thornwold to the_lamp).

thornwold_lamp_coal_told.description: The Lamp showed the player what is in the iron box: the last coal of the Spire's midwinter fire, broken into slivers for the waymark lanterns. When it is spent the lanterns go out.

thornwold_lamp_name_lost.description: The Lamp told the player it had another name once and 'put it somewhere' (forgotten). A Remnant candidate for the Ridge Light's burning.

thornwold_lamp_ladder_told.description: The Lamp admitted putting the ladder down after the fourth collier came up asking for a lantern, so there would be no fifth. The four went on north along the ridge.

thornwold_lamp_heard_of_aldous.description: Player told the Lamp what Brother Aldous confessed in Saltmarrow (reads saltmarrow_aldous_confessed; the Lamp recognises the sleeve-ember's stitching if the player carries it). The coal in the iron box went cold on one side the night of the Snuffing.

thornwold_lamp_heard_seventh.description: Told the Lamp (Wynn) what Aldous counted: six novices with names and a seventh light on the east landing with no face. The Lamp answers Aldous's sorry ('lamp') or weighs the player ('self').

thornwold_stair_light.description: What the player asked of the Lamp for the dark Keepers' stair: '' (not asked), 'sliver' (the Lamp broke a new sliver off the last coal - it shrinks), 'moved' (take the fourth waymark's lantern off the colliers' road - Hob's road gets darker) or 'refused' (the stair stays dark). Shifting paths: the woods' light follows the choice.

thornwold_fourth_lantern_taken.description: The player unhooked the lantern from the fourth waymark on the colliers' road (thornwold_stair_light=moved): that waymark goes dark and its pool of clear ground closes up.

thornwold_stair_lantern_hung.description: The player hung a Keeper's lantern on the bare waymark at the foot of the Keepers' stair (taking down the collier's cap that hung there): the stair stands in clear light.

thornwold_hob_has_cap.description: Player gave Hob Marl the felt cap from the stair's waymark: Ottie Swale's, one of the four colliers who went up after the Lamp. Hob keeps it on the cold hut's seat with the boots. Once Hob gives the boots away (thornwold_boots_away) the cap goes with them.

thornwold_boots_away.description: Hob Marl gave Ottie Swale's boots (and the cap, if he had it) to the player as a Remnant of his memory of the four colliers, for the Ridge Light. The cold hut's seat is bare while it is true; returning the unburned boots sets it false again. Stays true if they are burned.

thornwold_salt_row_away.description: Bram Kettle unpegged the SALT row from his tally board and made it a Remnant of the camp's memory of the colliers, for the Ridge Light. The board's bottom pegs are bare while it is true; returning the unburned stick sets it false again. Stays true if it is burned.

thornwold_beacon_burned.description: Which Remnant fed the Ridge Light: '' (unlit), 'boots' (Hob Marl's memory of the four colliers who went up after the Lamp — he stops waiting, the cold hut is nobody's) or 'salt_row' (the lumber camp's memory of the colliers and the salt trade — the camp will never know who brings the charcoal). Thornwold's burning; Thornwold forgets it for good.

thornwold_hob_came_in.description: After the Ridge Light was lit, a paid Hob Marl kept his promise and came in to the lumber camp by daylight (one-time arrival scene at the landing). Moves Hob from the clearing to the camp; Bram knows him unless the salt row burned.

thornwold_lamp_saw_light.description: Player has spoken with the Lamp after the Ridge Light was lit (one-time aftermath: the lanterns can go out now; what the coal is kept for).

thornwold_lamp_name.description: The Lamp's name carried home from the Tidewrights' Book (Day 45): '' (not yet), 'told' (the player said it outright: WYNN SALLOW; the Lamp puts its hood back, finishes its sentences, and remembers who told it to keep a coal back the last midwinter) or 'left' (asked first; the Lamp chose to leave it paid in the Book and stay the Lamp, for the four coming down the road).

thornwold_hob_ladder.description: The Fifth (Day 49; salt_row path only — Hob still keeps the four): '' (not yet), 'going' (asked to come up the ladder from the tally-house step, Hob went on ahead; he is off the step), 'up' (the ridge scene seen: the Lamp told him he is the fifth and offered him a lantern; he stands at the ladder's head with it, waiting on the player's word), 'gone' (told to go after the four: he walked north-east up the old Keepers' road with the lantern and hung it on the second bare waymark as he went by, so the next would know he'd gone up) or 'stayed' (told to stay at the bottom of the road: he built a mark by the tally-house step and hung the lantern on it, and cut four notches onto Bram's bare SALT pegs).

thornwold_hob_told_fifth.description: The Fifth: Hob came up the ladder and the Lamp told him he is the fifth, and gave him a lantern lit off the Ridge Light (one-time ridge arrival scene; moves thornwold_hob_ladder from 'going' to 'up').

thornwold_hob_stick_back.description: Pell gave Hob Marl his count-stick back at the tally-house step as he got up to go up the ladder ('Finders keep FOR. You want to know what you were counting now'). On the ridge Hob finishes the half notch.

thornwold_bram_heard_fifth.description: Player told Bram Kettle what became of the old collier on his step after The Fifth (one-time: gone up the ridge, or the mark at the bottom of the road and the notches on the bare SALT pegs).

fen_landed.description: The player has come ashore at Glasswater Fen's staithe (one-time arrival scene after the first sailing north-about from Thornwold).

fen_met_hesper.description: Player has met Hesper Vail, Unmoored warden of Stillhithe's staithe.

fen_ember.description: Asked by Hesper to cup the ember on Stillhithe ('it reminds'): 'cupped' (closed their hand over it) or 'bare' (refused). The Unmoored react to it.

fen_heard_of_dunstan.description: Hesper told the player about the big man who rowed to the fen, paid his mooring in whittled gulls, left his name with her and went out along the long walk into the Deeps. Starts The Letting Post.

fen_rowboat_seen.description: Player has looked at the Saltmarrow rowboat tied at Glasswater's staithe (Oda can then name its builder).

fen_dunstan_word.description: What the player left on the Unmoored's letting post for the big man further in: 'mara' (Mara's word: the stool's still by the door), 'own' (someone from Saltmarrow came looking) or 'none' (left nothing: the right to forget). Paid off when Dunstan is found at the end of the long walk (Day 37).

fen_hesper_saw_word.description: Hesper has remarked on what the player left (or didn't) on the letting post (one-time).

fen_met_corran.description: Player has met Corran Teal, the last of the fen folk, at his eel landing.

fen_corran_trap_asked.description: Asked again to be poled out to the Heron, Corran sent the player to lift his far trap at the end of the long walk, in the Deeps' fog, where he won't walk (he doesn't go where the Unmoored go).

fen_corran_decided.description: Corran has decided he likes the player (they lifted his far trap and brought it back; in it, the keeper's skiff bell) and will pole them out to the Heron Light.

fen_punt_out.description: The player is out at the Heron Light's legs in Corran's punt (Corran is there with them, not at his landing). Cleared when he poles them back.

fen_heron_reached.description: Corran has poled the player out through the channels to the Heron Light's legs at least once (the first trip is the full scene).

fen_dunstan_glimpsed.description: At the Heron's legs the player saw a big man with an unlit lantern standing at the edge of the fog on a tussock, looking at the water, before he walked off into it: 'called' (called his name; he stopped, didn't turn, went on), 'watched' (let him go without a word) or 'nameless' (after the gull burn: his name wasn't there to call). Pays off when Dunstan is found.

fen_skiff_bell.description: What the player did with the keeper's skiff bell Corran found in his far trap, at her skiff by the Heron's legs: 'hung' (tied it back on her bow) or 'kept' (kept it). When the Heron is lit the bell rings once by itself, on her bow or in the satchel.

fen_heron_ladder_seen.description: Player has looked at the Heron Light's ladder: the rungs above the slime scraped clean by boots, recently. Someone climbs it (Corran: 'I want a dry day, and you want a reason').

fen_hesper_heard_heron.description: Back from the Heron's legs, the player told Hesper about the trip (her answers follow the bell, the big man and the ladder). She tells them that some nights a small light goes up the Heron's ladder and comes down again: the reason to climb (A Light for Glasswater → up_the_ladder).

fen_heron_climbed.description: The player climbed the Heron's ladder with Corran holding the foot and found the lantern room: the cradle heaped with cold put-down things, a whittled gull on its rim, the keeper's coat folded on the boards. The cradle won't take what nobody holds (→ feed_the_heron).

fen_hesper_name_away.description: Hesper said her name out over the pool until it didn't come back, and gave it to the player as a Remnant (hespers_name) for the Heron. Cleared if the unburned name is given back.

fen_corran_cord_away.description: Corran held his knot-cord out in the fog till it went silver and gave it to the player as a Remnant (corrans_knot_cord): every channel he ever counted back. Cleared if the unburned cord is given back.

fen_beacon_burned.description: Which Remnant fed the Heron Light: '' (unlit), 'name' (Hesper Vail's name — the last thing she kept; she meets the boats without it) or 'channels' (Corran's knot-cord — nobody living knows the deep channels; the fen folk can't come home through them, and nobody poles out to the Heron again). Glasswater's burning; Glasswater forgets it for good.

fen_lantern_seen.description: Back on the fen after Glasswater's burning, the player saw the lantern lit at the fog's foot set down at the end of the long walk (one-time arrival scene; starts For After).

fen_dunstan_met.description: The player found Dunstan Tollen at the end of the long walk, sat on a tussock by his lit lantern, whittling, and he said his name (after the gull burn it slides off). Completes For After.

fen_dunstan_mara.description: What the player told Dunstan of Mara: 'message' (her word, in person or tied on the post — he whittled a gull for the stool, facing the door), 'burned' (that she says Tollens end with her and sets out two cups — the gull burn), 'spared' (after the gull burn, only that she's well), 'well' (that she's well) or 'nothing' (not theirs to carry).

fen_dunstan_rule.description: Whether the player asked Dunstan what he came to put down ('asked' — he doesn't know: 'that's how you know it went') or kept Stillhithe's rule ('kept').

fen_hesper_heard_dunstan.description: Hesper has been told the big man was found by his lit lantern (one-time): she keeps his name till he comes for it.

fen_oda_heard_heron.description: Oda has been told about the trip out to the Heron's legs (the bell, the big man) — one-time.

fen_oda_heard_dunstan.description: Oda has been told Dunstan was found (one-time): 'Is he laughing?'

saltmarrow_mara_got_gull.description: The player gave Mara the gull Dunstan whittled for her at the end of the long walk; she set it on his stool facing the door.

fen_oda_lane_asked.description: Oda told the player where the lane runs on from the lit fen: east-about to Wrackholm. Once Dunstan is found (the player 'done here') she'll sail it.

wrackholm_landed.description: First landfall at Wrackholm played (the arrival scene: the yard dark, the answering horn lashed). Starts A Light for Wrackholm.

wrackholm_met_wenna.description: The player met Wenna Garrow, lane-warden of Wrackholm, by the lashed horn and heard why nobody answers (a horn answered is a lane promised) and of the Gannet.

wrackholm_met_jory.description: The player met Jory Pask stripping the Gannet's copper in the yard.

wrackholm_board_read.description: The player held the ember to the Gannet's blank crew board and the chalk came back: Hale Corbet, master; Annis Corbet; Ruan Pask.

wrackholm_gannet_named.description: Wenna said the Gannet's crew's names into the lashed horn (The Gannet's Crew done), and told the player it was her answer brought them in.

wrackholm_jory_brother.description: The player told Jory his brother's name, off the crew board: Ruan Pask.

wrackholm_who_answered.description: What the player told Jory about who called the Gannet in: '' (not asked), 'wenna' (the truth: Wenna answered, and the Wrack went out), 'keepers' (the Spire was put out on purpose, by Keepers) or 'dark' (nobody's to blame for the dark). For Wrackholm's burning and the Tidewrights' arc.

wrackholm_wenna_saw_sleeve.description: The player showed Wenna the Keeper's sleeve-ember: Keepers pay twice, once for the crossing and once into the lane-house Book (their names).

wrackholm_book_told.description: Wenna told the player the Lamp's name may be in the lane-house Book of Keepers carried (if it ever rode a Tidewright deck); she'll find its page once the Wrack is lit.

wrackholm_wenna_offer.description: Wenna weighed the player's deeds (three lit) and offered to swear them a friend of the lanes once the Wrack is lit: the Tidewrights court the Wakebearer.

wrackholm_jory_float.description: Jory gave the player a glass float off the come-home pile for Pell's finding pouch (something lost, something good).

saltmarrow_pell_float.description: The player brought Pell the glass float from Wrackholm in the finding pouch: something lost, something GOOD. It sits on top of the lost-things crate.

wrackholm_teeth_marks_told.description: Wenna remembered that nobody ever knew the way across the Teeth by heart: you put your feet on the white, the lampwardens' white-lead marks, renewed every spring (the fog will have had them off). She sent the player to wait the spring tide down at the spit's end.

wrackholm_tide.description: The tide off Wrackholm's spit: '' (in: the Teeth under, the usual state) or 'low' (the bottom of the springs: the Teeth stand up out of the water enough to walk). Waited down at the spit's end; the flood comes back behind the player as they cross back from the Teeth. A local story value until day/night and tides exist as a system.

wrackholm_teeth_marks.description: At low water the player held the ember to the first rock off the spit and the lampwardens' white-lead marks came back, rock after rock out into the fog toward the Wrack: the way across the Teeth.

wrackholm_teeth_crossed.description: The player crossed the Teeth on the white for the first time (the crossing scene on reaching them).

wrackholm_jory_up.description: With the Gannet's copper off, Jory went up the shingle to Wenna, as he said he would once he knew it was her answer (who answered = wenna); he stands by her at the horn after.

wrackholm_board_leave.description: With the Wrack wanting feeding, Wenna (the yard) gave leave for the Gannet's crew board to be prised off her transom for it: a year and a tide, and nobody is coming for her now.

wrackholm_board_taken.description: The Gannet's crew board is off her transom (the player prised it off with Wenna's leave; it's in the satchel, or burned). Set back to false if the player puts it back unburned.

wrackholm_beacon_burned.description: What fed the Wrack Light (Wrackholm's burning): '' (not lit), 'answer' (Wenna's answer: nobody on Wrackholm remembers she ever answered a horn, the Gannet's night included), 'board' (the Gannet's crew board: the crew unnamed again on Wrackholm, for good) or 'white' (Hale's white-lead pot: Jory's one day out on the Teeth behind Ruan; nobody left on the island has walked behind a lampwarden).

wrackholm_horn_sounded.description: With the Wrack lit, Wenna cut the lashing off the answering horn and it was sounded (it takes two: Jory, if he came up, else the player); Oda's horn answered from the jetty if the ferry lay there.

wrackholm_book_opened.description: Wenna opened the lane-house Book for the player by lamplight. Its last line, the night of the Snuffing, is a name the fog has had, in a hand that wrote fast; nobody on Wrackholm wrote it or saw it written. The ember leaned to it and the player shut the Book without deciding to (mystery #2 hook; never explain yet).

wrackholm_lamp_name_read.description: In the lane-house Book, thirty winters back, the player read the Lamp's name in its own hand: WYNN SALLOW, keeper, for the Ridge Light. Paid twice. (To carry back to the Lamp.)

wrackholm_sworn.description: Wenna's offer, at the scale over the lane-house door once the Wrack was lit and the horn sounded: '' (not answered), 'sworn' (sworn a friend of the lanes: no Tidewright deck will weigh the player light) or 'declined'. For the Tidewrights' and Keepers' arcs.

lanes_oda_weighed_name.description: Oda has weighed the Lamp's name being carried home off the Book (one-time line at Thornwold landing once thornwold_lamp_name is set; differs for a friend of the lanes).
